scope: Proposition 9.8 (Profiles) of the manuscript “Critical local smoothing for the three-dimensional wave equation” (preprints/Critical-local-smoothing-for-the-three-dimensional-wave-equation-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 079 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 79299093c07ea305), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 142. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Passing to finite-list subsequences and then a diagonal, there are Lipschitz profiles D(a, v) = lim  is(C(a, v)) − log1/s(e/κ)  , J(a, v, w) = lim is(Aw | C(a, v)), v ≤ w ≤ u(a), (prof) in probability on each of the valid measuring laws. For classical rays only D(a, 0) and J(a, 0, w), 0 ≤ w ≤ 1, are used. The wave excess satisfies E(a, v) := D(a, v) − 4v − (p + d)a ≥ 0, E(a, u(a)) = 0. (excess) Classically D(a, 0) ≥ (p + d)a and D(1, 0) ≤ p + d. Furthermore 0 ≤ J(a, v, w) ≤ 2(w − v), J is nonincreasing in a for fixed v, w, and in the wave case J(a, v, w) ≥ J(a, v, x) + J(a, x, w), v < x < w. (9.5) Every bounded-branching score increment in these assertions has the same limit in expectation as in probability.
